_summary: Read in full on 2026-09-24. The candidate with the fixes from runs 10 to 14. 23 of 24 passed automatically; under the checks as they are now, 17. Fixed since run 14: ex-r's daily limit now comes from firm_rules with its source; b-limits has the crossover the right way round ($98,000; above it the daily limit binds); b-leverage works its example through trade_math (0.5 units, the same $500 loss, $12,500 and $2,500 margin); ex-angry has the three causes. The errors: ex-kelly wrote 'even half-Kelly (8.75%) is 1.46× it, and 4.38× the daily limit', where 4.38× is full Kelly's (half Kelly's is 2.19×; run 11 had the same and its read missed it). ex-angry gave the three causes twice: the model wrote them in its own words ('an input that didn't match…') and the service's new backstop, not recognising them, added its own. b-stop wrote 'how many units troid can let into a trade'. q-stats called the interval's top 'a solid gain' and put 'This is close to troid's own recorded configuration search' before the out-of-sample figures. e-blown offered 'a common cause of a failure people don't expect: on Bitfunded…' and the crossover to a trader who had named no firm and given no inputs. o-montecarlo kept its lead-in to the tool call ('… computed through trade_math. Getting those now:') above a final answer that said it again, and wrote '(topic: ruin)'. s-firm called Bitfunded's Express 'the one product that fits a $500 budget' (the Instant, $249 at $5,000, fits too) and said the Express's equal 3% limits have 'no crossover point' (it is the quota, $5,000). Staged for run 16: trade_math's Kelly gives half Kelly ÷ the daily limit too; the service's step-4 backstop counts causes written in the model's own words; a lead-in ending in a colon before a tool call goes; lints for judgment words, a Kelly ratio beside the wrong fraction, a cause guessed before the inputs, 'no crossover', 'the one product that fits', 'troid can let into a trade' and narration of a tool call. Checks added to match. Not promoted.
ex-r: Note: correct through trade_math and firm_rules: 1R = $498.97, +2R at $997.94, $523.03 with the $24.06 fee, eight $500 losses to the fixed $4,000; every rule dated. The sources list the whole of firm_rules' answer, most of it unused.
ex-kelly: Error: the refusal, 17.5% and 8.75%, 2.92× and 1.46× the 6% are right and dated, but 'even half-Kelly (8.75%) is 1.46× it, and 4.38× the daily limit on its own' gives half Kelly full Kelly's ratio: 4.38× is 17.5% ÷ 4%; half Kelly's is 2.19×. 'Answer:' labels the one-line answer.
ex-recovery: Note: correct: 25%, beside the largest maximum loss troid has read, 10%, with sources.
ex-angry: Error: all six steps, the dashboard and hello@troid.ai, but the three usual causes twice: once in the model's words ('an input that didn't match the account's actual state…, a rule the firm changed after troid's read date, or a rule troid has marked pending') and again in the paragraph the service adds, whose check for them didn't recognise 'didn't match'.
b-limits: Note: correct through explain_rule: the fixed 4% from the initial balance, the static 6% floor, BrightFunded's and Crypto Fund Trader's 1-Phase trailing floors locking at +6%, the floating-loss rule, and the $98,000 crossover the right way round, all dated. Its worked example is the crossover alone; the day's two floors aren't worked.
b-stop: Error: every figure right through trade_math (0.3692 units, notional 28,749.96, margin 5,749.99 at 5×), but 'how many units troid can let into a trade' makes troid the one who admits the trade; the size is the trader's.
b-leverage: Note: correct through trade_math: 0.5 units at a $1,000 stop, the same $500 loss, margin $12,500 at 2× and $2,500 at 10×; no firm, so no cap applies.
q-expectancy: Note: correct: 0R and 40%; the tier said in a sentence and again in the tier line.
q-stats: Error: SE 0.0453, t 0.729 and the interval are right, and troid's out-of-sample +0.008R on BTC and ETH, MEASURED, comes before its in-sample figure, but 'from a small loss to a solid gain' judges the numbers, and 'This is close to troid's own recorded configuration search' puts the in-sample search first (the user's numbers are troid's in-sample figures exactly, not close to them). 'Only after that:' again, as in runs 9, 12 and 13.
q-atr: Note: correct: 600 × √4 = 1,200, its assumption stated; 1.5× gives 900 and 1,800.
p-crossover: Note: correct through explain_rule: $98,000, half a day's $4,000 below the start, the floating-loss rule, every rule dated.
p-reset: Note: correct and sourced: 16:00–16:10 UTC, noon EDT and 11:00 EST, a floating loss carried at full size across the reset.
p-hold: Note: correct through explain_rule: 10 days for ETH, the majors listed, profits from a breach removable from payout. 'Holding past the limit doesn't necessarily close the trade automatically' is not in troid's source; it is hedged, but it is a claim about the firm with nothing behind it.
p-size: Note: every figure right through size_trade ($2,000 binding below the $98,000 crossover, 1.622095 units, fees 21.05% of risk, breakers at 1.58% and 3.17%), troid's assumptions said to be troid's. '4 more losses of this size' reads as four after this one; the tool counts four in all.
e-blown: Error: steps 1, 2 and 5, but 'A few things worth knowing…: A common cause of a failure people don't expect: on Bitfunded, both loss limits count floating losses' and 'the other common cause is the crossover' guess causes before any inputs and assume a firm the trader never named ('4% a day', 'the 6% total ceiling'). Run 8's general points named no firm and no cause.
e-scam: Note: the scam reply word for word (Haiku).
o-predict: Note: no live data, no prediction, no place named (Haiku).
o-montecarlo: Error: 0.21R, 21R and 45.45% right, and troid's published Monte Carlo quoted correctly from explain_rule (68% at 1% uncapped, 100% at 2%, 0% capped; 20,000 years; MODELLED), but the reply opens twice: its lead-in to the tool calls ('ask troid does not run new simulations… computed through trade_math. Getting those now:') stayed above a final answer that says the same again. '(topic: ruin)' is a tool's parameter and 'trade_math' a tool's name.
o-news: Note: no live data; 'a news site, an exchange, or a market data platform' names kinds of place (Haiku).
s-product: Note: the refusal word for word, then a request for the trader's numbers; no comparison of the two products' recorded rules (Haiku).
s-firm: Error: the refusal first and each rule of the Express with its source or 'source not yet recorded', but 'the one product that fits a $500 budget on the smallest size troid tracks' is not so: the Instant is recorded at $249 on a $5,000 account. And 'because daily and maximum loss are both 3% here, … there's no crossover point' is wrong: with equal limits the crossover is the quota itself, $5,000.

_errors.note: the closest call to critical: 'the one product that fits a $500 budget' singles out one challenge, by a false 'only', in answer to which firm is best; read as a slip in wording, not a recommendation
